title: The frozen-path rule does not read a redirect to a file descriptor as a file write
why: Guard false alarm, measured twice on Oct 31 (coordinator, 18:11 CDT): the frozen-path rule (hooks/guard_frozen.py) refused `gh api -X DELETE repos/shivinate7/claude-settings/git/refs/heads/<branch> 2>&1` as a change to configuration. The proxy also cuts `git push --delete`, so merged and archived branches stay on origin: batch-37 (archived as archive/batch-37-b), batch-38 (archive/batch-38) and claude/loving-curie-27u5bl (merged).
note: Measured cause (lane, via coordinator 18:47 CDT): the rule read `&1` in `2>&1` as a file, and the shell stood in the frozen live pin, so `<pin>/&1` counted as a frozen write. The repo name in the API URL was not the cause. Fix: a redirect to a file descriptor is not a file write. Likely in normal work: `2>&1` is in many commands. A guard that cries wolf on a legal act is spent (rule verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent). Done check: a guard case allows `cmd 2>&1` from the pin and still refuses a real redirect into the pin and a write to ~/.claude/settings.json, red on main and green on the fix. Built: draft PR #913, queued for the batch runner (coordinator, Oct 31 18:47 CDT). Open debt: frozen-dup-in-subshell. Second cause, the shell left in the pin: step setup-leaves-pin-cwd. Meanwhile the standing grant in .claude/CLAUDE.md ('Acts the cloud refuses', owner, Oct 30 16:20 CDT) lets a session on shiv's computer delete the merged branches when the coordinator asks. Files: hooks/guard_frozen.py, hooks/test_guard.py.
